To economize means to use something — most often money, but also resources, time, or effort — carefully and without waste, so that you use less of it than you otherwise would.

When you economize, you are making a deliberate choice to cut back, spend less, or avoid unnecessary use of something. It is a conscious, purposeful act of being careful and efficient with what you have.

Think of it this way: the opposite of economizing is being wasteful or extravagant. When you economize, you are actively working to prevent waste.

The idea at the heart of this word is efficiency with intention — not just accidentally using less, but choosing to do so.

1. Without specifying what you're saving (general use)

Here, "economize" simply means to reduce spending or cut back on expenses in a general way — to be more careful with money overall.

"After she lost her job, she had to economize."
(She had to start spending less and being more careful with money in general.)

"The government announced that all departments must economize."
(All departments must cut back their spending and avoid waste.)

2. With "on" — to economize on something (specific use)

When you say "economize on [something]," you are pointing to the specific thing you are cutting back on or using more carefully.

"They economized on fuel by turning off the air conditioner."
(They deliberately used less fuel.)

"The company economized on travel costs by switching to video calls."
(They reduced travel expenses specifically.)

"She economized on time by preparing her meals in advance."
(She used her time more efficiently and avoided wasting it.)

Although "economize" is most commonly associated with money, it can be used for any resource that you want to use carefully and efficiently:

  • Time — "We need to economize on time if we want to finish by evening."
  • Energy — "The new design economizes on power consumption."
  • Space — "The architect economized on space by using built-in furniture."
  • Words — "A good writer knows how to economize on words." (This means: say what needs to be said using as few words as possible — no unnecessary rambling.)

In all these cases, the word carries the same core idea: use less, use wisely, avoid waste.
The Feeling and Tone of the Word

This is important: "economize" is a neutral to positive word. It does not suggest that the person is greedy, cheap, or miserly. Instead, it suggests that the person is sensible, responsible, and wise in how they manage what they have.

Compare:

  • "He is stingy" — negative; suggests selfishness
  • "He economizes" — neutral/positive; suggests wisdom and care

You economize because circumstances require it (a tight budget, limited resources) or because you simply believe in not wasting things. Either way, there is no shame or negative judgment attached to the word.

People and organizations economize in situations like:

  • During a financial crisis or when income drops
  • When trying to save up for something
  • During a shortage (of fuel, water, electricity, etc.)
  • When a company wants to improve its profits
  • During wartime or emergencies, when resources are scarce
  • Simply as a personal habit of living within one's means
The Relationship Between "Economize" and Similar Words

• Save — Broader and more common in everyday speech. "I want to save money." "Economize" is slightly more formal and specifically emphasizes cutting back and being efficient, whereas "save" can also mean simply setting money aside.
  • Cut costs / cut back — These are informal, conversational equivalents. "We need to cut costs" = "We need to economize."
  • Be frugal — "Frugal" is an adjective describing a person who habitually avoids waste. "Economize" is the action — the thing a frugal person does.
  • Scrimp — To scrimp means to economize very harshly, often to an uncomfortable degree; it has a harder, more desperate feel. Economizing is calmer and more deliberate.

What it meansTo use money, resources, time, or effort carefully, cutting back to avoid waste
Used aloneGeneral belt-tightening: "We must economize."
Used with "on"Specific cutback: "Economize on electricity."
ToneNeutral to positive — responsible, sensible
What it is NOTBeing cheap, stingy, or miserly

In short: to economize is to be smart and intentional about using less — whether that's money, energy, time, words, or any other resource — so that nothing is wasted and you get the most out of what you have.
